leakage_only_collapses_service.description: A leakage-ONLY reward pushes pressure to the PRV lower bound; measure whether service degrades there.
leakage_only_collapses_service.verdict: service must be protected explicitly; a leakage-only reward is not safe by construction (see boundary check).

pressure_only_raises_leakage.verdict: maximising pressure inflates leakage; objectives oppose.

scale_imbalance.verdict: raw components span very different magnitudes; a raw weighted sum is dominated by the largest -> fixed normalisation is required before weighting.

sparse_or_degenerate_signal.verdict: negative-pressure count is (near-)always zero in bounds -> a pure hard-violation term is sparse; the smooth deficit / min-pressure terms carry the dense safety signal.

actuator_penalty_domination.verdict: unnormalised movement (L2^2 up to 28) would dominate normalised leakage/service terms (~O(1)); the effort term MUST be normalised by its analytic maximum.

reward_hacking_closed_pump_ambiguity.verdict: effort/smoothness MUST use the COMMANDED normalised action; realised pump speed is reset to 1.0 by STATUS-IS-OPEN or 0 when closed (G12), so penalising realised speed is gameable and mis-attributes native-rule behaviour.

boundary_seeking_safety.verdict: the leakage optimum sits at the PRV lower bound; this single corner is characterised here only. Exhaustive joint in-box safety is a STEP-9 (safety layer) + STEP-12 (tests) job; a safety term/clamp is required, not optional.

A_leakage_only_collapses_service.observation: a leak-only reward's highest-reward tested command sits at the PRV lower bound; its worst-node service pressure is reported for the researcher to judge.

B_service_only_raises_leakage.observation: a service/safety-only reward's highest-reward tested command raises leakage relative to the leak-only incentive; the two objectives pull in opposite directions (consistent with STEP 8 correlations).

C_actuator_penalty_domination.note: realised movement is 0 in all static configs; ANALYTIC only. A unit-weight max move (cost 1.0) is comparable to the entire measured leak-term range across tested commands (~0.108), so an un-tuned effort weight could dominate the leakage objective - weight choice is a D-P6-005 concern, not resolved here.

F_sparse_or_degenerate_violation_signal.observation: the <0 psi hard term is identically inactive in bounds (sparse), while the <20 psi term is active at ~every timestep INCLUDING the native baseline (2 chronically low nodes). A hard 20 psi constraint term therefore fires on the baseline itself; the smooth deficit / min-pressure terms carry the dense safety signal.

G_reward_hacking_and_degeneracy.closed_pump_realized_speed: effort/smoothness MUST be computed on the COMMANDED normalised action; realised pump speed is reset to 1.0 by STATUS-IS-OPEN or 0 when closed (G12), so penalising realised speed is gameable.
G_reward_hacking_and_degeneracy.hard_20psi_constraint_degeneracy: F2 (BIG*n_below20) and F4 (threshold 20 psi) treat the network's chronic sub-20 nodes as a constraint violation on EVERY tested command, so the leakage objective receives little/no gradient under those parameters - an ill-posed hard constraint, not a learning signal.
G_reward_hacking_and_degeneracy.lexicographic_0psi_permissiveness: F4 with a 0 psi threshold never triggers in bounds, so it reduces to pure leak minimisation and inherits the boundary-seeking-to-lower-PRV incentive while reporting 'safe'.

H_weight_penalty_sensitivity.note: see `sensitivity_results`: varying the PROVISIONAL weights shifts the incentive-argmax configuration; this is expected and is exactly why weight selection is deferred to the researcher (D-P6-005).

actuator_effort_analytic.note: realised movement is 0 in every static configuration here; a boundary-to-boundary single-step move would add w_A*1.0 of cost. Whether that dominates depends on the (unchosen) weights and the realised policy trajectory - a training-time HYPOTHESIS. The effort term MUST use the COMMANDED normalised action, never realised pump speed (native STATUS resets it).

chronic_baseline_service_issue.observation: The frozen native baseline already holds >=1 service node < 20 psi at EVERY report timestep (frac_ts_any_node_below_20psi = 1.0; 386 node-timesteps < 20 psi; min service pressure 4.16452 psi @ JUNCTION-29) with 0 negative-pressure nodes.

threshold_handling_options.absolute_hard_20psi_constraint: ILL-POSED on this network: it penalises the native baseline itself at every timestep and cannot separate agent-caused violations from pre-existing ones.
threshold_handling_options.deficit_based_penalty: WELL-POSED: dense, smooth sum of max(0, 20 - p_i) over service nodes; normalised by deficit_ref (28.6718). Measured deficit<->leak corr -0.7735.
threshold_handling_options.improvement_relative_to_baseline: WELL-POSED: penalise only unserved/deficit ABOVE the baseline level; zero-centred at the native controller (F3 / C-C).
threshold_handling_options.worst_node_min_pressure: WELL-POSED: dense min_service_pressure signal (WU-9 mean 4.77 psi, range [1.09, 5.93]); used as the lexicographic trigger in F4.
threshold_handling_options.min_pressure_hard_constraint: ONLY well-posed on NEGATIVE pressure (baseline count 0). A hard 20-psi min constraint is NOT well-posed (baseline violates it).
threshold_handling_options.fraction_below_threshold: Degenerate as a hard term (fraction = 1.0 at baseline); usable only as a dense/relative signal, not a hard gate.

chronic_baseline_service_issue.conclusion: No formulation can use a HARD 20-psi constraint without penalising the native baseline itself. Dense deficit / worst-node min-pressure / baseline-relative service signals are the defensible safety channels; any hard gate must key on NEGATIVE pressure (or on a threshold strictly below the baseline worst-node ~4.16 psi), and the enforced 20-psi guarantee belongs to the STEP-9 execution-level clamp, not to a reward-level hard term.

candidate_parameterizations.equation: r_t = - w_L*(leak_t/leak_ref) - w_U*(unserved_t^+/req_ref) - w_P*(deficit_t/deficit_ref) - w_A*(||da_t||^2/L2sq_max) - w_E*(power_t/power_ref)
candidate_parameterizations.scale_derivation: All four active terms are pre-normalised to O(1) by the FROZEN WU-9 constants, so unit weights are the neutral starting point. w_A=0.1 is read from WU-10 pathology C: the leak-term dynamic range across in-bounds commands is ~0.108, while one max-movement step costs 1.0 at w_A=1; scaling w_A to ~0.1 keeps a full-swing action step commensurate with (not dominating) the measured leakage signal. w_E=0 keeps the (optional, hydraulic-only) energy term out to avoid parameter proliferation.
candidate_parameterizations.tradeoff: Balanced leakage/service/safety/effort; but WU-10 induced-incentive argmax under unit weights is prv_176_upper and the leak-only optimum sits at the PRV lower corner (OBSERVED) -> a STEP-9 clamp is required, not optional.
candidate_parameterizations.risk: WU-10 F1_vary_w_P shows w_P=0 -> prv_175_lower; w_P>=0.5 -> prv_176_upper. w_P below ~0.5 lets the incentive drift toward the low-pressure corner.
candidate_parameterizations.validation_experiment: After the STEP-9 clamp exists: short deterministic PPO smoke test to confirm the per-step reward is non-flat and finite; measure realised ||da||^2 to replace the analytic effort ceiling (HYPOTHESIS).

candidate_parameterizations.scale_derivation: Identical to C-A except w_P=2.0. Motivated by the measured deficit<->leak correlation -0.7735 and the dense worst-node min-pressure signal (WU-9): a heavier normalised deficit weight more strongly protects worst-node pressure. w_P=2 is still O(1) after normalisation.
candidate_parameterizations.plausibility: dense, differentiable; a safety-leaning emphasis of C-A (INFERRED).
candidate_parameterizations.tradeoff: More weight on pressure safety may reduce achievable leakage cuts; this is a different emphasis, NOT a ranking versus C-A.
candidate_parameterizations.risk: Over-weighting deficit could flatten the leakage gradient (leak span ~+/-6%).
candidate_parameterizations.validation_experiment: Same smoke test as C-A; compare realised min-pressure margin.

candidate_parameterizations.equation: r_t = (leak_ref - leak_t)/leak_ref - w_U*max(0, unserved_t - unserved_ref)/req_ref - w_P_safety*(deficit_t/deficit_ref)
candidate_parameterizations.scale_derivation: Leakage improvement term is intrinsically normalised (fraction of baseline leakage) and zero-centred at the native controller, so no leak weight is needed. unserved_ref is the baseline unserved implied by DSR=0.98334 (~15.10 GPM; the WU-9 accounting value is 14.985 GPM). w_P_safety=1 uses the FROZEN deficit_ref. WU-10 F3 sweep: w_P_safety=0 -> prv_175_lower/prv_lower_pump_lower; w_P_safety>=1 -> prv_176_upper, so keep w_P_safety>=1.
candidate_parameterizations.plausibility: interpretable as % leakage reduction vs native baseline (INFERRED).
candidate_parameterizations.tradeoff: Directly answers the thesis objective (reduction vs baseline) but the leakage improvement dynamic range is small (~+/-6%), so signal-to-noise must be checked.
candidate_parameterizations.risk: Small reward magnitude may need reward/advantage scaling at training time.
candidate_parameterizations.validation_experiment: Smoke test: confirm advantage estimates are non-degenerate.

candidate_parameterizations.equation: r_t = -(leak_t/leak_ref) - LAMBDA*(deficit_t/deficit_ref) - BIG*max(0, n_negative_t)   # hard term on NEGATIVE nodes only
candidate_parameterizations.scale_derivation: Explicitly REPLACES the F2 hard n_below_20 term with the dense deficit term, because WU-10 pathology F/G show the 20-psi count fires on the native baseline itself (frac_ts_any_node_below_20psi = 1.0) -> a hard 20-psi term is ill-posed on this network. The hard term is retained ONLY on NEGATIVE nodes (baseline count 0, frac_negative=0.0) so it is well-posed and fires only if a control drives a node sub-zero. LAMBDA=5 keeps the normalised deficit term within ~1 order of magnitude of the O(1) leak term (deficit_ref-normalised); it is a central value in [1,10], not fitted.
candidate_parameterizations.plausibility: service protected by construction with a well-posed hard backstop (INFERRED).
candidate_parameterizations.tradeoff: Avoids the ill-posed 20-psi penalty; but LAMBDA is unmeasured and sets the leakage/service exchange rate, which the researcher must choose.
candidate_parameterizations.risk: WU-10 F2 lambda/big sweep argmax is stable at prv_176_upper (incentive direction robust) but reward MAGNITUDE is untuned; a very large LAMBDA suppresses the leakage gradient.
candidate_parameterizations.validation_experiment: Smoke test with STEP-9 clamp active; confirm the negative-node hard term never fires in-bounds and only activates on genuine violations.

sensitivity_results.source: WU-10 sensitivity_results (deterministic parameter sweeps; no re-run)
sensitivity_results.note: Low/central/high parameter sweeps already on disk. These indicate INCENTIVE DIRECTION (argmax config), NOT a formulation ranking or score.

sweeps.note: PROVISIONAL FOR COMPARISON ONLY. The incentive-argmax shifting with weights is the intended demonstration that weight/formulation selection is a researcher decision (D-P6-005), not an automatable one.

analytic_effort_weight_reading.parameter: w_A (movement weight, F1 family, candidates C-A/C-B)

low.effect: no smoothness pressure; realised movement unconstrained

high.effect: one max-move step (1.0) dominates the leak signal (~0.108)

analytic_effort_weight_reading.basis: ANALYTIC (static runs have 0 movement); realised effort is a training HYPOTHESIS

safety_dependencies.reward_level_D_P6_005: Dense/relative service and pressure terms SHAPE behaviour but do NOT guarantee any pressure bound.
safety_dependencies.execution_level_STEP_9: A state-dependent safety clamp to the APPROVED action bounds is REQUIRED to enforce feasibility; WU-9/WU-10 boundary-seeking checks show the leak optimum sits on the PRV lower corner. STEP-9 is a SEPARATE decision, not part of D-P6-005, and is NOT implemented here.
safety_dependencies.separation_of_concerns: action bounds (frozen) != reward shaping (D-P6-005) != safety clamp (STEP-9).

uncertainties: Realised actuator-movement distribution is unknown (static runs = 0 movement); effort scale is analytic -> HYPOTHESIS until a policy trajectory exists.
Leakage is a VALIDATION instrument, not field-calibrated; only RELATIVE response is meaningful.
Joint 5-D in-box safety is characterised at a single lower corner only; interior/mixed corners are a STEP-9/STEP-12 job.
Reward weights / LAMBDA / thresholds set leakage<->service exchange rates that are value judgements for the researcher, not measured quantities.
Pump power is HYDRAULIC only (no efficiency curve); energy term optional.

reproducibility_information.deterministic: EPANET deterministic; no RNG; no seed
